summary: Each turn you flip cards from a shared deck into the harbor, deciding when to stop before a repeated ship busts your haul, then either bank the coins or spend people cards to buy more people or complete expeditions for points. It plays fast and tense, with real competition to snipe the person or expedition cards you need before an opponent takes them.
praised: Quick, tense push-your-luck decisions every turn
Very portable, low table footprint, easy to teach
Meaningful tension between greed and safety on each draw
Card-sniping/drafting adds real interaction despite the simple core loop
criticised: Can feel like multiplayer solitaire when the harbor stays safe
Luck of the draw can swing outcomes regardless of skill
Little to do on other players' long push-your-luck turns
Limited long-term strategy depth for heavier gamers

interaction.kind: open drafting and card sniping for people/expeditions

scoring.why: Points come mainly from the people cards you've hired (with set-collection bonuses for color variety) plus expedition cards you've completed
